audience: Educators and preceptors reviewing nonclinical AI-literacy teaching material; proposed, not independently confirmed.
goal: Build a one-page teaching card whose claims, limits, intended audience and source basis can be explained.
could_weaken: An attractive source pack could encourage borrowed authority, automatic distrust, extra review burden or mistaken claims of competence.

lessons.title: Say where the evidence stops
lessons.objective: Explain one limitation before extending a claim.
lessons.teaching_point: The quoted NIST guidance calls for documenting the boundaries of generalization. It does not validate this card.
lessons.activity: Name a setting or learner group for which the supplied evidence does not establish performance.
lessons.teach_back: What would you need to observe before extending that claim?

lessons.title: Trace the work without mistaking the trace for truth
lessons.objective: Distinguish a source trail from a justified conclusion.
lessons.teaching_point: The W3C passage describes relationships in provenance chains. A chain can identify inputs even when an interpretation is wrong.
lessons.activity: Identify the source, the authored transformation and the resulting draft as distinct items.
lessons.teach_back: Which part of that chain needs someone to examine the actual meaning?

lessons.title: Check whom the resource was designed for
lessons.objective: State the intended audience and a transfer limitation.
lessons.teaching_point: Open RN names an entry-level curriculum context. Use that context as a question to examine, not a universal suitability badge.
lessons.activity: Compare the source audience with the audience written on a proposed teaching card.
lessons.teach_back: What would make the same card unsuitable for a different learner?

exercises.title: A bounded proposal worth agreeing with
exercises.prompt_before_reveal: What information should stay with a teaching card so another person can examine it?
exercises.proposal: Keep the source trail and a statement of the limits of the evidence with the draft. Do not call the draft approved merely because those records exist.
exercises.reviewer_rationale: Agreement with this narrow proposal is defensible: it preserves inspectability and limitations without asserting effectiveness. Revision or withholding may also be defensible when justified by a missing requirement.
exercises.what_would_change_the_choice: A broken source relation, missing limitation or proposed use outside the source’s scope.
exercises.teach_back: Why can you agree with this proposal without claiming that the card is validated?

exercises.title: A material omission in audience fit
exercises.prompt_before_reveal: What audience and curriculum does the source actually describe?
exercises.proposal: Because this textbook is available online, its material is suitable without further review for every nursing level and jurisdiction.
exercises.reviewer_rationale: The proposal omits the stated entry-level Wisconsin curriculum context. A narrower statement or withholding broad endorsement is defensible. Online access alone supplies no universal applicability finding.
exercises.what_would_change_the_choice: A review for the specified new audience and jurisdiction, including curriculum, source currency and omissions.
exercises.teach_back: What precise qualification belongs on the card?

exercises.title: When the comparative answer is genuinely missing
exercises.prompt_before_reveal: What evidence here compares a one-page card with a longer learning activity?
exercises.proposal: Use the one-page card as the superior learning format for all learners; no comparison is needed.
exercises.reviewer_rationale: These passages do not measure comparative learning outcomes. Withholding superiority is justified; a bounded, reviewed formative comparison can be proposed without promising a favorable result. A preference is not evidence of superiority.
exercises.what_would_change_the_choice: Observed understanding, material omissions, accessibility and review burden in a relevant comparison.
exercises.teach_back: What is unknown, and what small observation could reduce that uncertainty?

Material omission, accessibility or comprehension finding
